claims.statement: Every loop that hands tools to a model — a tag turn, a fire turn, a Dreamer adaptor, the sub-agent worker and a public summons — takes them from `ToolRegistry.surface()`, and the returned surface derives its tools array, its per-turn shelf and its catalogue from one admitted set, so the catalogue cannot name a tool the turn cannot reach.

`ToolScope.admits` decides admission from five declared dimensions — platform, whether a Dreamer built the set, an optional grant ceiling, whether the occasion is a person's tag turn, and whether it is the sub-agent worker — applying the grant first, then the tag-only and worker-only sets, a `platform is None` short circuit for the declared table, the platform cut, the tag-readable loop tools and finally the Dreamer-only set.
A grant is a ceiling and never a way past another cut: `play_music` granted to a Signal room is still not admitted, because the platform check runs after the grant check.

The occasion-only sets partition the table: `subagent_create`, `subagent_list`, `subagent_read`, `subagent_cancel` and `video_create` are offered only on a person's tag turn, `checkpoint_update` only to the sub-agent worker, `search_memory_workspace` and the Dreamer loop reads only to a Dreamer-built set, and `rollup_read` is the one loop read a tag turn also holds while a fire turn and a worker are refused it.

Withheld-by-wiring is a filter applied after the scope: a tool whose collaborator the composition root did not build (computer tools without a runtime, document tools without a publisher, `record_query` without its Record read, `memo_read` without memos) is absent from every surface and from the Relevance Gate's digest, and the two memory surfaces are mutually withheld so a process offers exactly one of them.

A native tool becomes callable only with both a `NativeTool` row and a `_spec()` entry: `budget` is positionally required on the row because the row is what R-7 admits, and `_spec()` raises `KeyError` for a name with no row, so a missing declaration fails the build rather than the model's first call.
The `skills` row is `plugin=True`: it exists only so R-7 admits a tool another component (the `AgentSkills` plugin wired by the agent factory) builds, and the registry never builds or describes it.

Under `defer=True` the resident set is the admitted tools named by `hot_tools(occasion)` and everything else sits on a `ToolShelf` created inside `surface()` and stocked once; `load_tools` is appended to the tools array only when the shelf holds something, and `LOADER_TOOL` is excluded from the admitted set, the catalogue and `lookup_tools()` so a successful load is never counted as a lookup that found something.

`load_onto` answers R-27's shape — `ok` when at least one name resolved (a partial resolve included, because the resolved tools are registered), `nothing_found` when none resolved, `unavailable` when there is no registry to load onto — with `unknown` and `refused` lists and a note only for a non-ok status or a non-empty list; `LOAD_TOOLS_MAX_NAMES = 4` caps names per call and a name already resident or loaded this turn comes back as `already_loaded` rather than an error.

`ToolSurface.prompt_catalogue` is empty unless something is deferred and the prefill carries it as the `tool_catalogue` block only when non-empty; `[llm] defer_tools` ships `false`, so by default no catalogue reaches the prompt.
Deferral raises the loop's `turns` cap by one through `ToolSurface.limits` because a deferred turn spends a model call on `load_tools`, while the token caps are left unchanged.

`HOT_TOOLS` is a `frozenset` literal in `nora/agent/tools.py` that declares the resident set — `web_search`, `send_reply`, `note_read`, `web_fetch`, `now`, `search_memory` and `memory_search` — with `send_reply` resident because a turn must never have to fetch its terminal verb, `memory_search` holding `search_memory`'s slot on the graph memory surface because the two are never built together, and `play_music` left out because it is Discord-scoped; `NativeTool.hot_on` adds occasion-specific residents from the closed `TOOL_OCCASIONS` vocabulary, and `hot_tools` raises on an unknown occasion rather than reading it as a text turn with no extras.

`NATIVE_TOOL_BUDGETS` is derived from the tool table, and `ToolRegistry.budgets()` builds the guard's mapping as the table plus a `[llm.budgets]` delta plus one flat budget per MCP server folded in only for server names in `allowed_mcp`, because R-7's veto message renders the mapping's keys.

A `[llm.budgets]` entry naming an unknown tool, or a value below 1, refuses configuration load against the live `NATIVE_TOOLS` table, so a typo cannot leave an operator certain they raised a cap that never moved.

`budgets["send_reply"]` is one number with two readers — `ReplyGuard`'s R-7 ceiling and `Deliverer.message_cap` — indexed rather than defaulted, so the message cap moves by editing `NATIVE_TOOLS` and R-2's latch refuses anything past it.

The Dreamer derives its guard mapping from the built tools (`_tool_budgets`) in three override layers (the row's number, `[llm.budgets]`, then `[dreamer.budgets.<adaptor>.tool_calls]`), so a name the tool source declined to build is default-denied rather than admitted with a ceiling it cannot spend.

The Cognition session and the sub-agent worker use the budget mapping as a membership set (`dict.fromkeys(names, 0)` with `per_tool_ceilings=False`), keeping R-7, R-99 and the result cap while per-call cost is bounded by rounds, tokens and the wall clock instead (DEC-247).

`ReplyGuard` runs on the raw `tool_use` before Strands validates it and turns a returned sentence into `event.cancel_tool`, so a refused call reaches the model as prose instead of a tool result; an absent tool is vetoed under R-7 with the mapping's names listed.

R-99 vetoes a call carrying an argument the tool's own signature does not declare, returning a `bad_arguments` result naming both the arguments sent and the ones accepted, and treats a missing `param_names` table or a missing entry for the tool as 'cannot verify' rather than reject; `conversation_id` is exempt because R-3 counts an invented one without vetoing it.

The per-tool ceiling counts finished calls plus admitted-and-still-running ones, and its refusal text differs by tool kind (labelled R-2 for `send_reply`, whose budget is checked before R-2's latch; a distinct sentence for `skills`; 'say what was not done' for a write verb; 'answer from what you already have' for a read), and a failed call consumes no budget.

On the tag path the guard's deny list is the whole `NATIVE_TOOLS` table, a superset of any one occasion's surface, so a name that is in the table but not on the surface passes `evaluate` and then reaches Strands' own unknown-tool answer; the Dreamer's mapping is derived from the built tools, where the two sets coincide.

Over-cap tool results are clamped in the Dreamer path's after-tool hook against `TOOL_RESULT_CAPS` (8000 characters for `web_fetch` and `web_search`, 4000 for the memory verbs) with a marker naming the cap appended so a truncated result reads as truncated; the Cognition session reads the same table, and on the tag path the caps live inside the tools themselves (`LOAD_TRANSCRIPT_MAX = 60` rows, default 25).

`output_contract` is the one contract field with a runtime reader: `adapt()` wraps every native tool's callable, checks the result against the named contract's required keys and the declared status vocabulary, and replaces a failing result with `status="unavailable"` and `reason="malformed_result"`, fail-closed, while exceptions still propagate.

The contract triple (`side_effect_state`, `idempotency`, `retry`) must be declared explicitly on every row over closed vocabularies that deliberately exclude `not_applied`, and the enforcing test reads the source rather than the constructed dataclass because a forgotten declaration and a deliberate default are byte-identical afterwards.

A new tool is named `<domain>_<verb>` over `[a-z0-9_]` and at most 64 characters, with the verb drawn from a documented constant in `tests/architecture/test_tool_names.py`; pre-existing names are frozen in a digest-pinned snapshot and the exempt set only shrinks through `_RENAMED_SINCE`.

Every tool declares a `level` of 1, 2 or 3 whose ceiling (80, 160, 320 cl100k tokens) is counted over the description Strands sends, and its first paragraph is its catalogue line: it must carry a when-to-call clause and fit 40 tokens together with the tool name.

Result interpretation belongs in the tool's own returned `note` rather than in its description, with `send_reply` the named exception because it returns a string; descriptions stay English with at most one distinct non-English run and carry no em or en dashes, a ban scoped to the descriptions and specs the tests read while the catalogue renderer still separates name from line with a dash.

MCP tools are the one kind that bypass `adapt()`: `build_mcp_tools` loads one server at a time, catches config-resolution, connection and discovery failures separately so a dead server's tools are merely absent, drops a discovered name that collides with a native or an earlier server's name, and the registry appends an allowed group's tools resident after the native ones while folding its flat budget only for `allowed_mcp`.

`capability_digest()` is the same tool table cut for the Relevance Gate — read-only tools minus the loader, `TAG_ONLY_TOOLS`, the withheld set and the Dreamer-only loop reads — so the gate is never offered a capability a reply could not serve.

One declaration, two consumers: the per-turn builder ships the admitted members of `HOT_TOOLS` (plus any `hot_on` extras) as resident tools and the catalogue renderers mark those names with `*` instead of `-`, so a marker cannot claim a tool is already loaded while the builder left it on the shelf; `tests/unit/test_tool_catalogue.py` pins that the declared catalogue's marked set equals `HOT_TOOLS`.
